result.title: Streaming Recurrent Memory
result.summary: Natural intelligence learns from a continuous stream of sensorimotor experience: data can arrive at high bandwidth, and behavior adapts to feedback as soon as it arrives, even when it is delayed. In contrast, most modern deep learning systems rely on stored datasets, replay buffers, and retained contexts through which credit is later assigned. At high data rates, storing and revisiting past experience can be impractical under tight memory and computational constraints. This paper studies recurrent memory under a streaming learning constraint: the learner learns from experience as soon as it arrives without storing raw experience. We ask whether a streaming learner can maintain a state that remains useful for future prediction and control from delayed feedback. We introduce Streaming Recurrent Memory (SRM), a recurrent memory designed for the streaming setting which preserves information that may matter later while remaining trainable with one-step backpropagation through time (BPTT). SRM provides a streaming-compatible recurrence that is designed to recall past information by content or time, track elapsed steps, and compose transformations whose outcome depends on the order in which inputs are observed. Across controlled memory tasks and streaming applications, SRM learns effectively with one-step BPTT, outperforming recurrent baselines in associative recall and online language modeling while achieving near-perfect success in associative T-Maze with delayed rewards. These results suggest that fixing how inputs are stored in the recurrent state, while learning how that state is read out, enables effective streaming learning without long-range backpropagation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Streaming Recurrent Memory（SRM），在不能存储原始经验的流式设定下设计循环记忆状态，使其可按内容或时间回忆、跟踪步数并组合顺序相关变换，且仅用一步 BPTT 训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定写入状态、学习读出」及延迟反馈下维持可用状态的做法，可能为 LVR 的潜在状态维护、轨迹训练与信用分配提供可核查线索，但论文本身并非视觉或多模态工作。
